ov: Two species of huge, shaggy wild cattle: the American bison, often called buffalo, and the European bison, or wisent. The American bison fell from about 60 million to just 541 animals by 1889.

why.dg: Among the most dangerous animals in North American parks: in Yellowstone, bison injured three times as many people as bears did in 1980–1999.
why.et: It was the principal food of the Plains peoples of North America.

ht: Up to about 1.9–2 m at the shoulder (American bison)
rg: North America (American bison) and Europe (European bison).

cf.tip: The American bison is often called a buffalo, but it isn’t one of the true buffalo.

fx: The European bison was once extinct in the wild; its IUCN status has since improved to Near Threatened.
